steps.tx: **Polyarteritis nodosa** or PAN is a systemic necrotizing vasculitis that selectively affects medium-sized and small muscular arteries. A defining clinical hallmark is that PAN characteristically **spares the pulmonary arterial circulation** and microvasculature such as postcapillary venules and glomeruli, demonstrating **no association with ANCA** autoantibodies.
steps.say: Polyarteritis nodosa is a necrotizing arteritis of medium and small muscular arteries. It characteristically spares the pulmonary vasculature and has no association with ANCA.

vis.alt: Polyarteritis nodosa angiographic and histological characteristics
vis.caption: PAN targets medium-sized muscular arteries while sparing pulmonary circulation and glomeruli. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: The **2022 ACR/EULAR classification criteria** for polyarteritis nodosa require biopsy confirmation of necrotizing arteritis or angiographic aneurysms or occlusions. Patients must accrue **5 or more points** across weighted domains including mononeuritis multiplex, motor neuropathy, testicular pain, livedo reticularis, renal insufficiency, and unexplained abdominal angina.
steps.say: The 2022 ACR and EULAR criteria require at least 5 points for classifying polyarteritis nodosa. Key criteria include mononeuritis multiplex, testicular pain, and livedo reticularis.

vis.alt: Diagram classifying vasculitis by vessel size with large, medium and small vessel examples.
vis.caption: Vessel-size classification placing polyarteritis among medium vessel disease. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: Secondary polyarteritis nodosa is historically associated with active **Hepatitis B virus** infection in up to 30 percent of cases worldwide. Circulating **HBsAg-anti-HBs immune complexes** deposit in arterial branching bifurcations, typically presenting acutely within the first **6 months** following acute HBV acquisition.
steps.say: Secondary polyarteritis nodosa links to acute Hepatitis B infection. Circulating hepatitis B immune complexes deposit in arterial walls within 6 months of acute infection.

nodes.label: Acute Hepatitis B viral infection with high viral load
Vessel wall deposition causing secondary necrotizing arteritis

steps.tx: Renal involvement in PAN is driven by necrotizing arteritis of the main, lobar, and arcuate renal arteries, causing downstream renal cortical infarction and severe renin-mediated **renovascular hypertension**. True **glomerulonephritis is absent** in PAN because glomerular capillaries are small vessels completely spared by the disease.
steps.say: Renal disease in PAN stems from renal arteritis causing severe renovascular hypertension. Glomerulonephritis is absent because glomerular capillaries are spared.

right.title: Glomerular preservation in PAN
points: Absent glomerulonephritis and red cell casts

steps.tx: Visceral catheter angiography or CT angiography provides decisive diagnostic images, demonstrating characteristic **microaneurysms of 1 to 5 mm** and segmental stenoses at branching bifurcations of the renal, mesenteric, and hepatic arteries. This classic vascular distortion produces the diagnostic **beads-on-a-string** angiographic sign.
steps.say: Catheter angiography demonstrates classic microaneurysms measuring 1 to 5 millimeters. The resulting beads on a string appearance is diagnostic.

nodes.label: Transmural necrotizing inflammation weakens internal elastic lamina
Pulsatile stress causes focal aneurysmal outpouchings (1 to 5 mm)
Alternating saccular aneurysms and stenoses show beads-on-a-string pattern

steps.tx: Gastrointestinal involvement presents with postprandial **abdominal angina**, bowel ischemia, transmural infarction, and life-threatening visceral perforation. Mesenteric ischemia represents the leading cause of death in severe polyarteritis nodosa, constituting an automatic adverse score on the **Five-Factor Score** that mandates aggressive cyclophosphamide and high-dose corticosteroid therapy.
steps.say: Mesenteric arteritis presents with postprandial abdominal angina and bowel infarction. Gastrointestinal involvement carries high mortality on the Five-Factor Score.

steps.tx: First-line induction therapy for severe idiopathic PAN with a **Five-Factor Score of 1 or more** combines high-dose systemic glucocorticoids with **intravenous cyclophosphamide**. Conversely, mild non-organ-threatening disease with a Five-Factor Score of zero can be managed initially with oral glucocorticoid monotherapy alone.
steps.say: Severe idiopathic polyarteritis nodosa requires high-dose corticosteroids combined with cyclophosphamide. Mild disease without poor prognostic factors responds to steroids alone.

left.title: Severe PAN (FFS >=1)
points: Pulse methylprednisolone followed by high-dose oral steroids
Transition to azathioprine or methotrexate maintenance

right.title: Mild PAN (FFS = 0)
points: Escalate to cyclophosphamide if disease progresses

steps.tx: Management of **HBV-associated PAN** differs fundamentally from idiopathic disease. Treatment combines a short, time-limited course of corticosteroids and **plasma exchange** alongside immediate antiviral therapy with **entecavir or tenofovir**. Long-term cytotoxic immunosuppression must be strictly avoided as it promotes uncontrolled viral replication and fulminant hepatic failure.
steps.say: Hepatitis B-associated PAN requires antivirals entecavir or tenofovir with short-term plasma exchange. Long-term cytotoxic immunosuppressants are avoided to prevent hepatic necrosis.

nodes.label: Immediate potent oral antiviral therapy (entecavir or tenofovir)
Short-course corticosteroids and plasma exchange to clear immune complexes
Strict avoidance of long-term cytotoxic cyclophosphamide
